evidence_slot_schema.note: Observations are produced by the named query/artifact and stamped at read time. The aggregate matrix is a static linkage, not a synchronization trace.

WB1-DISPOSITION.artifact_or_query: select plan_number, status from nebula.implementation_plans where plan_number in ('0002','0005','8261653') + GET /state
WB1-DISPOSITION.source_reference: winning receipt kind in nebula.receipts_unified + vision.tickets row

WB2-TICKET-CLASS.artifact_or_query: select plan_id, role, status, count(*) from vision.tickets group by 1,2,3

WB3-SWEEP-LOG.artifact_or_query: select id, plan_id, role, status, expires_at from vision.tickets where status in ('open','claimed','stale')

WB4-GATING.source_reference: this spec file + nebula.receipts_unified derived status

WB6-GENERATION.artifact_or_query: select plan_id, role, position, status from resolution.ticket order by plan_id, role, position (fallback vision.tickets)

WB6-REJECT.artifact_or_query: select kind, payload->>'scope' from resolution.receipt where kind='review_reject'

generation_projection.invariant: /state exposes all open ticket generations; a closed older-generation row never hides a newer open row of the same role. Canonical ticket/receipt stores stay authoritative; /state is a projection.
required_semantics: project per (plan_id, role) by generation position, not by row order
expose the newest generation per role
report any open/claimed generation that is not the newest as hidden_open_generations (a defect signal, never a silent collapse)
generation_projection.live_defect: watcher.getState() builds a role-keyed ticket map with ORDER BY plan_id, role and no generation ordering (M6)

expiry_audit.invariant: Conduit core owns expiry semantics; the sweeper is the enforcement mechanism. Every generation, including REVIEW_REJECT rework, receives a durable expiry transition/audit event at expires_at. Expiry never implies completion; an expired unclaimed implementation ticket re-alerts/returns according to the reject scope.
required_semantics: for each non-terminal (open/claimed/stale) generation past expires_at emit exactly one audit event
the event carries plan_id, role, generation, expires_at, from_status, to_status=expired, reason=expiry_detection, implies_completion=false
expiry_audit.live_defect: 171 expired tickets vs 84 expiry_detection events; 574 terminal tickets with zero transition events (M8)

reject_routing.invariant: Classify REVIEW_REJECT by scope. scope=implementation routes to a builder rework ticket; scope=blueprint routes to a Planner re-scope/repair event, not another builder ticket, preserving the original evidence and stopping the builder->review->reject loop until the Planner response is recorded.
required_semantics: classify the latest REVIEW_REJECT by its structured scope field
scope=blueprint emits a Planner re-scope/repair event and creates no builder ticket
scope=implementation emits a builder rework ticket
absent scope resolves to the documented default implementation
blueprint return preserves the original evidence and stops the builder->review->reject loop until the Planner response is recorded
reject_routing.live_defect: all 338 review_reject receipts carry no scope; every reject resolves through the implementation default (M9)

stop_condition.decomposition: W-B1..W-B6 are linked through the package registry and the aggregate evidence matrix; each is independently reviewable; and no open builder ticket can claim the unsatisfiable end-state AC, because the end state is not in this plan's scope. Runtime Conduit/Nebula agreement is delegated to the child execution WorkRequests and is evidenced only by their filled slots.
stop_condition.open_builder_ticket_guard: A builder ticket may claim a package's implementation slice only when its own start conditions are met. It may never claim the wave end-state AC (Conduit/Nebula runtime agreement); that claim is reserved for the child execution WorkRequests and their evidence slots.

delegation.runtime_agreement: child execution WorkRequests per package (docket c7c26160); this blueprint's conformance harness is not runtime evidence
